title: Filet Mignon with Red Wine Pan Sauce
subtitle: butter-basted tenderloin steaks, a glossy red wine sauce and garlic mashed potatoes
imageAlt: A seared filet mignon with red wine pan sauce beside creamy mashed potatoes on a cream plate with a navy napkin

breakdown: Milk, garlic, onion, oil, salt, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: Take the steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and pat them very dry.
Use an oven-safe skillet: the steaks go from the stove into a hot oven.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold salted water, boil and simmer 15 minutes until very tender. Drain, mash with the milk, butter, grated garlic and salt, and keep covered.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Season the steaks with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high until shimmering and sear 3 minutes a side until deeply browned.

steps.title: Baste and roast
steps.text: Add the butter and smashed garlic, tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks 30 seconds. Move the skillet to the oven for 5–8 minutes, until 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare or 71°C (160°F) for medium.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest the steaks on a plate, loosely tented, 5 minutes.

steps.title: Pan sauce
steps.text: Pour off all but 1 tbsp fat (careful: the handle is hot). Cook the onion over medium 1 minute, add the wine and boil, scraping, until reduced by half, 2–3 minutes. Add the broth and boil 3 minutes until syrupy. Off the heat, swirl in the cold butter.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate the steaks on the mash and spoon the sauce over.

fixIt.fix: The pan wasn't hot enough or the steaks were damp; dry them well and wait for the oil to shimmer.
Take the pan off the heat before adding the butter, and swirl, don't boil.
Pull them 3°C before your target; they rise while resting.

saleTip: Buy a small whole beef tenderloin roast on sale and cut your own steaks; freeze the rest.
swap: Striploin or top sirloin steaks (sear only, 4–5 minutes a side). Beef broth with 1 tsp balsamic vinegar for the wine.
leftovers: Slice cold leftover steak thinly for sandwiches.
doneness: Whole cuts of beef to 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare or 71°C (160°F) for medium (Health Canada).
source: Based on tested restaurant-style filet mignon methods (Serious Eats, Canadian Living): sear, butter-baste, finish in a 200°C oven, then a reduced red wine pan sauce mounted with butter.
prepAhead: Make the mash ahead and reheat with a splash of milk.
Dice the onion and measure the sauce before searing.
reheat: Leftover steak: slice and warm gently in a covered pan, or eat cold. Mash to 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Seared steaks and garlic mash with garlic butter; no wine sauce.

stepNotes.4: Basic: skip the sauce; spoon the pan butter over the steaks.

fancy.note: Bacon-wrapped filets and buttery green beans.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: wrap a bacon slice around each steak and secure with a toothpick before searing; sear the bacon edge 1 minute too.

addSteps.title: Green beans
addSteps.text: Boil the beans 4 minutes, drain and toss with the butter and a pinch of salt.

plating: Mash swooshed with the back of a spoon, steak on top.
Sauce around, not over the crust.
Candles, cloth napkins, the good glasses.

why.1-0: Tenderloin is the most tender cut, and a thick steak gives a crust without overcooking the centre.
why.2-3: Cold butter swirled in at the end makes the sauce glossy.

funFact: 'Filet mignon' means 'dainty fillet' in French, but in France the cut is usually called tournedos.

keeps.note: best fresh; cooked tenderloin goes dry

drink: A Cabernet Sauvignon or Malbec, or a pomegranate spritzer.
